doubts.why: a plain h, without the mark below that he gives both h-signs elsewhere in the article: read X, his sign 15 of 1911 (the closed readings differ here)
a plain h at the end of the article's text, where the same word has ḫ in § 16 (teñkelḫe): read X as printed
a numeral printed "1·2" (his summary: "1-2 women"): read as two numerals, 1 and 2
the last digit is hatched in the print (damaged): kept as a lost sign
"Mnê" ends a printed line and "teslke" begins the next, without a hyphen: kept as two words
his footnote on the lost sign: "Perhaps a numeral"
his footnote mark on the lost sign before it, the note "Perhaps a numeral"
his footnote: "Probably confused for alleleb-šê, cf. l. 13"

notes: Typed by hand from page images of Griffith's article (public domain; the JSTOR copy on Zenodo, record 2497984), not from its text layer. He prints the text in 21 sections (§§ 1-21) that run on from l. 1 to l. 42; this row runs them together in the order of the stela. text_std: his letters and marks, with (N) for the start of line N of the stela. text_corpus: the corpus spelling (ê o, š S, s s, ñ N, z d, ḫ x, ẖ X), his word division, his restorations kept as letters, '.' a lost sign. lines: the words of text_corpus by the line of the stela each starts on. doubts: the words he marks with '?' or '(?)', then the places we are unsure of. src/akinidad.py writes this row from data/expansion/jea/griffith1917_rem1003.txt.
